messages.subject: SECR advice for continuous data-set
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm still learning the ropes of SECR and want to check I'm on the right track.

I have nearly 3 years of continuous camera trap data on a species with natural markings, however this data is split into three different studies (same general site, but different camera locations and survey efforts). E.g.:
Study 1 = 15 months of continuous data
Study 2 = 6 months continuous (following on from Study 1, but cameras in different locations)
Study 3 = 12 months (continuous again, but different/more camera locations to study 2)

I'm mainly just interested in calculating density for this species for each study period. Is 15 months too long of a period? The population would not be considered 'closed' over this time, however. I tried estimating separately over month-long periods, but the estimates were crazy inconsistent, with some having massive CIs and s.e. I think this is due to low no. of detections (or repeat detections of individuals) over these shorter time-frames, which skewed estimates.

I've run code for each of the three Study periods (detection histories were created in camtrapR). An example of one is below:

SCRIPT
>summary(SDH_Study1) #summary of capthist
>suggest.buffer(SDH_ Study1)
>buffer <- suggest.buffer(SDH_ Study1)  # in metres
>secr.0 <- secr.fit(SDH_ Study1 , model = list (D ~ 1, g0 ~ 1, sigma ~ 1), buffer = buffer)
>secr.0

OUTPUT

>From this density estimate is 38 indv / 100km2 (?), which makes sense for my site. Estimates were also quite similar for each Study. Does all this look right? Am I missing any basic modelling or considerations? Is there a better way to split up my data?

Any advice would be excellent!

Thanks
Tim

messages.body_plain:
You can expect a lot of pushback from some quarters if the duration of your nominally 'closed' sampling spans potential recruitment etc. (see literature on Indian tigers). I think the risk has been overstated, but you are taking it to an extreme.

As I understand, you have 33 months of sampling of more or less the same population using a camera configuration that changed radically at two points in time. This could be treated as one analysis with a large camera array in which some locations were unused for periods of time (as coded in the 'usage' attribute of the detector array). However you would still need to handle non-closure. For that the choices I see are (i) slice the 33 months into acceptable intervals (3 months?) and treat each as an independent session in 'secr', or (ii) also slice the data into sessions, but fit an open model in openCR that allows for possible turnover.

Option (ii) is formally better and may make better use of the data, but goes against my own recent advice that for density estimation you're on safer ground with closed models. Option (i) loses some recaptures (these are precious) and tends (slightly) to overstate the precision because the same animals are treated falsely as novel random events in successive sessions.

Either way you're stuck with some tricky data manipulation.

Diana
Getting sense from CJSsecr requires that you set details = list(CJSp1 = TRUE). Did you do that? This peculiarity is (hidden?) in a footnote on p3 of the vignette, and explained in Section 7.2 and Appendix E of Efford & Schofield (2020).
Also, to estimate population trend you need to fit a model with recruitment at least a PLBsecrX (=JSSAsecrXCL) model, where X is f, l, etc. Are you confusing lambda (population trend) and lambda0 (detection intercept)? It would help to see your actual code.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Error running secr.fit
messages.body_plain:
Hi Josh
That error comes from verify() and can be avoided by setting verify=FALSE in the call to secr.fit. Then you will encounter a problem with initial values (because the first session has no captures from which to infer the detection scale). You can get around that by including details = list(autoini = 14). Then it's just very slow... You don't need to be told this, but the data are rather thin as there are only 3 recaptures at more than 20 metres. I wouldn't bother with session-specific densities, and I would be looking to speed up fitting by tuning the masks (reduce buffer <=250 m, set spacing, say 15 m?) and perhaps discretizing the polygons (but that doesn't work with empty sessions in the current version).
Murray
